Histological analysis showed fascial sclerosis, lymphocytic, plasma cell, and eosinophilic infiltration of the fascia, and muscle and interlobular septae of panniculus. panels.rationale: Single clinical photograph of a patient demonstrating inability to oppose the palms due to hand tenosynovitis, the stated prayer sign. In this disease-focused case report, this is a specific musculoskeletal manifestation of eosinophilic fasciitis and corresponds to the allowed progressive flexion contractures finding.
panels.attribution_text: Servy et al. Eosinophilic fasciitis: a rare skin sclerosis.. Pathology research international 2010. doi:10.4061/2011/716935. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Prayer sign due to hand tenosynovitis.
in_text_mentions: Physical examination revealed symmetrical lesions of dermal sclerosis with normal superficial skin. Prayer sign due to tenosynovitis of the hand (Figure 1), venous furrowing (“groove sign” or “le signe du canyon” in France, Figure 2) of the wrist, and arthritis in the feet and knees were noted. We saw no telangiectasia, calcinosis, megacapillary, sclerodactyly, or mucosal involvement. The patient showed neither Raynaud phenomenon nor digital ulceration.
